objective: To spell irregular past-tense verbs that change their vowel
defs: moved quickly on foot; past of run
made music with the voice; past of sing
moved through water using the body; past of swim
took liquid into the mouth; past of drink
made a clear bell sound; past of ring
rested on a surface; past of sit
jumped suddenly upward or forward; past of spring
held on tightly and would not let go; past of cling
pierced with a sharp point; past of sting

sentences.ran: She ____________________ all the way to the bus stop but arrived two seconds after it pulled away.
sentences.sang: The choir ____________________ so beautifully that three members of the audience started to cry.
sentences.swam: He ____________________ the full length of the pool without coming up for air until he touched the wall.
sentences.drank: After the long hike, they ____________________ the spring water as if they had never tasted anything so good.
sentences.began: The storm ____________________ quietly enough, but by midnight every tree in the garden was bending double.
sentences.rang: The school bell ____________________ just as the teacher was about to give out the results of the test.
sentences.sat: The cat ____________________ perfectly still on the windowsill, watching the birds on the lawn below.
sentences.sprang: The goalkeeper ____________________ to the left and managed to push the penalty just past the post.
sentences.clung: The kitten ____________________ to the top branch with all four paws, refusing to come down for two hours.
sentences.stung: A bee ____________________ him on the finger as he reached into the lavender bush to smell the flowers.

starter.question: Can you change these verbs to the past tense? What do you notice?
starter.ruleBox: Ablaut: these verbs change their vowel to make the past tense — no -ed needed. i → a: sing→sang, ring→rang, swim→swam. u → a: run→ran. Two go i → u: cling→clung, sting→stung.

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Think of the base verb for each word. What happens to the vowel?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words are past tenses of irregular verbs. Instead of adding -ed, the vowel changes: sing→sang, swim→swam, ring→rang. Linguists call this ablaut — an ancient vowel shift inherited from Old English. Most follow i→a, but clung and stung go i→u, and run→ran goes u→a. No -ed is ever needed.

clicks.label: Base word
clicks.body: singan — to sing; related to German singen

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: singan was the Old English infinitive. The past tense sang is one of the oldest verb forms in the language.

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Old English strong verbs changed their vowel for the past tense. Singan → sang follows the i→a pattern of Class III strong verbs.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We still use sang as the simple past of sing: 'she sang a lullaby to the baby.'

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: The i→a pattern runs through today's words: sing→sang, ring→rang, swim→swam, drink→drank. Linguists call this vowel change ablaut.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box1sub: The vowel in the past tense becomes a short -a- sound
wordSort.box2sub: The vowel changes to -u- (i→u) or from u→a
wordSort.hint: Look at the vowel in each past-tense word. Is it an -a- sound or something different?
wordSort.answerNote: Vowel → -a-: sang, swam, drank, began, rang, sat, sprang. Other change: ran (u→a), clung (i→u), stung (i→u).
wordSort.exampleLine: sing → sang (i→a) | sting → stung (i→u) | run → ran (u→a)

wordShed.def: started to do something for the first time
wordShed.sentence: The explorer began her journey in the dark, long before the rest of the village had woken up.
wordShed.morphology: begin (v) → began (past) → begun (past part) → beginning (pres part) → beginner (n) → beginners (pl n)
